mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime restrictions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is observed, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tightening labor market that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation environments (CPIAUCSL > 202.0), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 202.0, the signal (FEDFUNDS rising) fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 signals manufacturing weakness that reduces corporate profits, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days without regime restrictions.
failure_condition: RSAFS rising fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% signals monetary tightening that increases discount rates for equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.
